$description.$value: Core primitive tokens for Nango. Neutral ramp aligned to the actual Nango app charcoal grays (warm-neutral, not zinc). Brand and info both use the Nango cyan-blue ramp (#00B2E3 family — from webapp index.css). Success uses Nango green (#4CD964 family), warning uses Nango yellow (#F7C752 family), danger uses Nango red (#EE4242 family). Geist for UI text, Geist Mono for code/data. Primitives are shared across themes — semantic files resolve them per mode.
Shared primitive color palette sourced from the Nango webapp CSS (packages/webapp/src/index.css).
Absolute anchors.
Transparent for ghost/overlay states.

Warm-neutral charcoal ramp. Light end fixed for clear visual steps: 0=#FFF, 25=#FAFAFA, 50=#F5F5F5, 100=#EBEBEB, 200=#E0E0E0. Dark stops: 975=#000 (canvas), 950=#0B0B0C (page), 925=#121212 (panel), 800=#2A2B2F (overlay). Sourced from Nango webapp charcoal palette.

925-50.$description: neutral.925 at 50% opacity — for alert.bg in dark mode.

750.$description: AA-safe brand stop, added to fix the primary button. .700 (#0089B0) is the marketing/website blue but only reaches 4.03:1 with white text — fails WCAG AA (4.5:1). .800 (#016886) passes at 6.31:1 but reads as dark teal, drifting from the brand cyan. At .750, white text hits 4.78:1 (AA pass with margin) while staying visibly closer to brand.500 (#00B2E3) than .800 does. Used as the single interactive.primary fill in BOTH Light and Dark themes so the button no longer changes hue between modes.

975.$description: Extra-dark stop — used for alert/banner bg in dark mode where .950 is too saturated.

$description.$value: Nango brand cyan — the single source of truth for blue in the system. Brand 500 (#00B2E3) is the canonical Nango cyan, used for brand identity (logo, marketing surfaces). Interactive UI (buttons, links, focus rings, selected states) uses color.info, which aliases per-stop to color.brand — one blue, two semantic names. Primary button fill and selectedFill both resolve to brand.750 (#007CA0), the AA-safe stop added so white text clears 4.5:1 in both themes; .500 itself is not used directly for interactive fills. Update .500 to shift the base hue, or .750 to adjust interactive contrast.

950-50.$description: brand.950 at 50% opacity — for status.info.bg in dark mode.

975.$description: Extra-dark stop — used for alert/banner bg in dark mode where .950 is too saturated.

$description.$value: Aliased to color.brand. There is one blue in the Nango system — the brand cyan — and color.info exists only as a semantic name for interactive UI (buttons, focus rings, links, selected states, info alerts). Update color.brand to change the blue everywhere. Focus shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(0,178,227,0.2).

950-50.$description: brand.950 at 50% opacity — for status.info.bg in dark mode.

750.$description: AA-safe icon stop, added to fix icon.success reading too dark in light mode. .700 (#1E9E3E) is the vibrant success green but only reaches 2.93:1 on surface.panelInset (#EBEBEB) — fails the 3:1 UI-component threshold on that one surface. .800 (#1A6B2C) passes everywhere (5.53–6.60:1) but reads as a muddy dark green, losing the 'healthy/connected' visual signal — this is what caused the light-mode 'icons look very dark' report. At .750, contrast is 3.29:1 on panelInset and 3.93:1 on white/page — clears 3:1 with margin on every light surface while staying visibly closer to the vibrant .700 green. Mirrors the color.brand.750 precedent (added for the same reason on the primary button). Used as the single status.success.icon value in Light theme.

975.$description: Extra-dark stop — used for alert/banner bg in dark mode where .950 is too saturated.

$description.$value: Success ramp — connected, healthy, complete states. Sourced from --color-green-* in webapp index.css. 500=#4CD964, 700=#1E9E3E, 750=#1D943A (icon-only AA-safe stop), 900=#0A3D16.

950-50.$description: success.950 at 50% opacity — for status.success.bg in dark mode.

650.$description: Closest stop to warning.500 that still clears 3:1 on every light surface — added 2026-07-09 per request for a less-brown, more-yellow icon color. Holds warning.500's hue and saturation (H≈43°, S≈91%) and darkens lightness only as far as needed: 3.12:1 on surface.panelInset (the tightest surface), 3.72:1 on white. .700 (#A07B10) is the same hue family but noticeably less saturated/lighter-shifted, which is what read as 'brown' rather than yellow. Any lighter than this (toward .600 #E6B738) drops below 3:1. Used as the single status.warning.icon value in Light theme.

975.$description: Extra-dark stop — used for alert/banner bg in dark mode where .950 is too saturated.

$description.$value: Warning ramp — caution, degraded, retry, non-blocking alerts. Sourced from --color-yellow-* in webapp index.css. 500=#F7C752, 650=#AC7C08 (icon-only, closest-to-500 AA-safe stop), 700=#D6A81E, 900=#5C4A0B.

950-50.$description: warning.950 at 50% opacity — for status.warning.bg in dark mode.

550.$description: Muted/desaturated meter-only stop — added 2026-08-28 per Erick's review comment that the Billing & usage 'Compute time' limit bar read as too aggressive at danger.500. Same hue as the rest of the ramp (H=0°) but desaturated from 83.5% to 62.4% and darkened slightly (L 59.6%→54.1%) — this is NOT an interpolation between .500 and .600 (both of those hold ~82-83% saturation); it's a deliberate desaturation off the ramp's curve, the same kind of move as brand.750/success.750/warning.650. Contrast: 4.56:1 on white/surface.panel, 4.37:1 on neutral.25/surface.page, 3.83:1 on neutral.100/surface.panelInset (light track), 4.11:1 on neutral.925/surface.panel, 4.31:1 on neutral.950/surface.page, 3.61:1 on neutral.875/surface.panelInset (dark track) — clears the 3:1 non-text/UI-component minimum everywhere with margin, actually beating the old danger.500 on the light track (3.21:1) and light panel (3.82:1). Used as meter.fill.exceeded — do not reuse for buttons, alerts, or status badges, which keep the vivid .500/.700 stops.

975.$description: Extra-dark stop — used for alert/banner bg in dark mode where .950 is too saturated.

$description.$value: Danger ramp — errors, failures, destructive actions. Sourced from --color-red-* in webapp index.css. 500=#EE4242, 700=#E81818, 900=#5A0F0F. Focus shadow for error states: 0 0 0 3px rgba(238,66,66,0.2).

950-50.$description: danger.950 at 50% opacity — for status.danger.bg in dark mode.

$description.$value: Alpha color primitives for overlays and borders.

Decorative-only accents for charts, avatars, tag differentiation. Sourced from --color-blue/violet/mint/pink/yellow-500 in webapp index.css. Never use for interactive states or status semantics — use info/success/warning/danger for those.

500.$description: Decorative yellow for chart series and categorical data. Same hex as warning.500 by design (Nango brand yellow), but lives in the accent namespace so charts don't reference the semantic warning ramp. Use warning.* only for actual caution/degraded states.

$description.$value: Primitive typography tokens. Geist for UI text, Geist Mono for code, IDs, API keys, slugs, and data.

mono.$value: Geist Mono, ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, Liberation Mono, monospace

$description.$value: 4px-base spacing scale. Half-steps (0_5, 1_5, 2_5, 3_5) ordered inline.
Corner radius scale. radius.lg (8px) matches the nango.dev --radius-main.
Border width primitives.
Icon size and stroke primitives.
Transition duration and easing primitives. Default transition duration in the Nango app is 100ms (--default-transition-duration).
Box-shadow layering tokens. Note: Token Studio boxShadow type requires inline rgba — cannot reference color.alpha primitives directly.
Opacity scale — covers both element opacity (disabled, subdued) and alpha-layer composition.
Blur tokens for overlays and softened backgrounds.
Responsive layout primitives. Breakpoints sourced from webapp CSS (--breakpoint-xl: 1280px, --breakpoint-2xl: 1440px, etc.).

Fixed widths for form controls (text inputs, selects/dropdowns, and similar single-line fields). Pick the size that matches the expected content length, not the width of the surrounding container -- see [[app-shell-content-grid-spec]] content-type rule (constrained content should never Fill).
Nango semantic tokens — Dark theme. Mirrors the Light structure exactly; only values differ.
Background and container surfaces.

raised.$description: NEW: lifted active surface. In dark, this is meaningfully different from panel.

$description.$value: Text colors.

muted.$description: A11Y RULE: do not use at fontSize.2xs (11px) or fontSize.xs (12px) — 4.18:1 on surface.panel, 3.68:1 on panelInset. Use text.secondary at those sizes. See 'Accessibility note — text.muted at small sizes'.

placeholder.$description: NEW: dedicated placeholder-text token, mirrors Semantic/Light.json's text.placeholder. Was reading as text.default/text.secondary in inputs, which made placeholder copy indistinguishable from real typed content ('too strong, confused with real text'). One stop past text.muted (toward the background) so it sits clearly below every real-text tier while staying legible — 3.12:1 on surface.input (#121212). Caveat: 2.93:1 on surface.inputMuted (readonly-style inputs) — just under 3:1; accepted since placeholder rarely appears in that variant and the ramp has no stop between .500/.600. Intentionally under the 4.5:1 text threshold: placeholder is a hint, not required reading (WCAG 1.4.3 does not apply to it), but stays close to 3:1 so it doesn't disappear. Do not use for real input values, helper text, or error text — use text.default/text.secondary/text.danger for those.

disabled.$description: A11Y FIX (2026-07-09): was neutral.600 (2.93:1 on the disabled button fill, and that gap shrank further once the fill was lightened — reported as unreadable). Moved to neutral.500 (same stop as text.muted) — 3.16:1 against the new interactive.disabled fill (neutral.800).

onBrand.$description: Flipped from neutral.900 to white — required now that interactive.primary/selectedFill use info.750 (dark text on info.750 only reaches 3.68:1, fails AA; white reaches 4.78:1).

linkActive.$description: UPDATED (2026-08-13): hover token removed from the link family (hover now renders with the default token); active stays at .600, darker than the .300 default per the darker-on-press rule. .600 (#009CC8) clears 5.88:1 on surface.panel, 6.17:1 on page, 6.59:1 on canvas — comfortably above AA, though with less margin than default since the info ramp gets darker (and lower-contrast against a dark surface) faster past this point.

linkNeutral.$description: NEW (2026-08-17): base color for the neutral/link-style button — alias to text.secondary so it matches what the component already rendered before this token existed. Added for parity with link/linkDanger/linkSuccess/linkWarning, which all have a named base token.

linkNeutralActive.$description: NEW (2026-08-17): active-state fix — previously default/hover/active all rendered as text.secondary with no distinct active feedback. Aliased to text.strong (neutral.900 light / neutral.50 dark) to mirror how every other link variant (linkActive, linkDangerActive, linkSuccessActive, linkWarningActive) gets a visibly darker/stronger stop for active. Contrast: 17.59:1 light (panel), 17.18:1 dark (panel).

linkDanger.$description: NEW (2026-07-22): dedicated token for danger-colored link/button-style text (e.g. the arrow 'Button' link component), separate from text.danger/status.danger.* so it doesn't drag the Alert along with it. text.danger (.400) read as too light for this use. .500 (#EE4242) clears AA on every dark surface tested — 5.49:1 on canvas, 5.15:1 on page, 4.90:1 on panel — while still being a vivid, clearly 'danger' red.

linkDangerActive.$description: UPDATED (2026-08-13): hover token removed from the linkDanger family (hover now renders with the default token); active stays at .700, darker than the .500 default per the darker-on-press rule. KNOWN, ACCEPTED AA MISS: danger.700 (#E81818) reaches 4.58:1 on surface.canvas only — 4.29:1 on surface.page and 4.08:1 on surface.panel both fail the 4.5:1 AA text minimum. This is the deepest stop before the ramp jumps into a fill-tuned dark-maroon register (.750/.800, which fail even more severely as text). Accepted deliberately for the darker-on-press rule; if this reads as too low-contrast in practice, the fallback is reverting active to a lighter stop (danger.300 passed AA everywhere) rather than hunting for a darker-but-legible stop, since none exists on this ramp.

linkSuccess.$description: NEW (2026-08-13): success variant of the link/AlertButton family, mirroring text.linkDanger. Aliased to text.success (success.400) — 11.39:1 on surface.panel, 9.48:1 on status.success.bg (the tinted alert surface an AlertButton sits on). No hover token: the link hover tokens were removed on 2026-08-13; hover uses the default token.

linkSuccessActive.$description: NEW (2026-08-13): active/pressed state for text.linkSuccess, darker than default per the darker-on-press rule. success.600 = 7.47:1 on surface.panel and 6.22:1 on status.success.bg — unlike the danger ramp, the green ramp has enough headroom to darken and still clear AA everywhere (success.700 would drop to 4.47:1 on status.success.bg, under AA, so .600 is the deepest safe stop).

linkWarning.$description: NEW (2026-08-13): warning variant of the link/AlertButton family, mirroring text.linkDanger. Aliased to text.warning (warning.400) — 12.60:1 on surface.panel, 8.33:1 on status.warning.bg. No hover token (removed family-wide 2026-08-13).

linkWarningActive.$description: NEW (2026-08-13): active/pressed state for text.linkWarning, darker than default. warning.600 = 9.99:1 on surface.panel, 6.61:1 on status.warning.bg — passes AA everywhere. The next darker stop (warning.650) collapses to 3.33:1 on status.warning.bg, under AA, so .600 is the deepest safe stop.

danger.$description: SWAPPED (2026-08-12): was danger.400 (6.71:1 on surface.input). Now aliased to border.danger (danger.500) per design request, so Input error label/description and the error stroke render as the exact same red. Still passes AA here — danger.500 on surface.input (#121212) = 4.90:1. SIDE EFFECT: if Alert Title reads from this token in dark mode too, its color changes from danger.400 to danger.500 — worth a visual check against status.danger.icon.

$description.$value: Borders and dividers.

inputHover.$description: A11Y/VISIBILITY FIX (2026-08-12): was alpha.white.50 — resolved only 1.4x the resting border's contrast against surface.input (3.84:1 → 5.36:1), reported as not enough visual separation between default and hover (weaker jump than Light's equivalent fix). Moved to alpha.white.64 (resolves to ~7.97:1 on surface.input #121212, 2.08x the default) — now matches Light's hover contrast almost exactly (7.93:1), so the hover state feels consistent across themes. See border.input for the resting value.

danger.$description: FIX (2026-08-12): was {color.danger.600} (#EB2D2D, 4.42:1 — already passing). danger.500 (#EE4242) = 4.90:1 against surface.input (#121212), still passes comfortably, and now matches Light.json so the token can't drift apart between themes again.

disabled.$description: A11Y FIX (2026-07-09): was alpha.white.6 (imperceptible against a near-black fill). Doubled to alpha.white.12 so the disabled button has an actual visible edge — on par with border.default (white.10) and still well below border.stronger (white.24).

$description.$value: Icon colors.

disabled.$description: A11Y FIX (2026-07-09): was neutral.600 (low contrast against the disabled fill, matched the old text.disabled report). Moved to neutral.500 to match the text.disabled fix — 3.16:1 against the new interactive.disabled fill (neutral.800).

link.$description: NEW (2026-08-12): icon color for the link/button component's leading or trailing icon (e.g. the arrow in the 'Button' link). Aliased directly to text.link — not to a color primitive — so the icon always matches the link text color exactly, in every theme, with a single source of truth.

linkActive.$description: NEW (2026-08-12): active-state pair to icon.link. Aliased to text.linkActive.

linkNeutral.$description: NEW (2026-08-17): aliased directly to text.linkNeutral, matching the icon.link/icon.linkDanger/etc. convention so the icon always matches the link text color exactly.

linkNeutralActive.$description: NEW (2026-08-17): active-state pair to icon.linkNeutral. Aliased to text.linkNeutralActive.

linkDanger.$description: NEW (2026-08-12): danger variant of icon.link, for the destructive/danger link-button icon. Aliased to text.linkDanger so icon and text stay identical.

linkDangerActive.$description: NEW (2026-08-12): active-state pair to icon.linkDanger. Aliased to text.linkDangerActive.

linkSuccess.$description: NEW (2026-08-13): success variant of icon.link, for the AlertButton icon. Aliased to text.linkSuccess so icon and text stay identical, same single-source pattern as icon.link/icon.linkDanger.

linkSuccessActive.$description: NEW (2026-08-13): active-state pair to icon.linkSuccess. Aliased to text.linkSuccessActive so icon and text stay identical, same single-source pattern as icon.link/icon.linkDanger.

linkWarning.$description: NEW (2026-08-13): warning variant of icon.link, for the AlertButton icon. Aliased to text.linkWarning so icon and text stay identical, same single-source pattern as icon.link/icon.linkDanger.

linkWarningActive.$description: NEW (2026-08-13): active-state pair to icon.linkWarning. Aliased to text.linkWarningActive so icon and text stay identical, same single-source pattern as icon.link/icon.linkDanger.

info.$description: DEPRECATED — aliased to status.info.icon (was {color.info.400}). status.*.icon is the single source for semantic icon color; verified >=3:1 on tinted status bgs AND neutral surfaces in both themes. Re-bind layers to status.info.icon, then remove this alias.

success.$description: DEPRECATED — aliased to status.success.icon (was {color.success.400}). status.*.icon is the single source for semantic icon color; verified >=3:1 on tinted status bgs AND neutral surfaces in both themes. Re-bind layers to status.success.icon, then remove this alias.

warning.$description: DEPRECATED — aliased to status.warning.icon (was {color.warning.400}). status.*.icon is the single source for semantic icon color; verified >=3:1 on tinted status bgs AND neutral surfaces in both themes. Re-bind layers to status.warning.icon, then remove this alias.

danger.$description: DEPRECATED — aliased to status.danger.icon (was {color.danger.400}). status.*.icon is the single source for semantic icon color; verified >=3:1 on tinted status bgs AND neutral surfaces in both themes. Re-bind layers to status.danger.icon, then remove this alias.

$description.$value: Solid fill colors for buttons, switches, selected states.

primary.$description: Unified brand-blue fill — same value used in Light theme, so the primary button no longer flips between bright cyan (dark) and dark teal (light). White text (text.onBrand) reaches 4.78:1.

dangerHover.$description: A11Y FIX (2026-08-12): was {color.danger.600} — a genuine AA failure, not just a style mismatch. .600 only reaches 4.25:1 for the white button label (text.onBrand), under the 4.5:1 text minimum, because on this fill+white-text pattern a *lighter* stop means *less* contrast (opposite of how it works for text-on-background tokens like text.link, where a lighter dark-mode stop pops more). Moved to the same new color.danger.750 stop added for Light theme's dangerHover fix — .750 clears 6.05:1, and keeps light/dark using one consistent hover value instead of diverging (light: darker-on-hover; dark: previously lighter-on-hover, which is what caused the AA miss here). Gives a smooth 700 (4.59:1) → 750 (6.05:1) → 800 (8.02:1) contrast progression through default/hover/active.

selectedFill.$description: Matches interactive.primary (info.750) so selected state and primary button read as the same brand blue. text.onBrand (white) passes at 4.78:1 — verified in both themes.

$description.$value: Global interactive state layers.

disabled.$description: A11Y FIX (2026-07-09): was neutral.900 (1.12:1 against surface.panel/page — fill was indistinguishable from the app background). Moved to neutral.800 (same stop as surface.overlay) for a visible recessed fill; combined with the border.disabled and text.disabled bumps, the disabled button now reads as a muted-but-legible control instead of disappearing into the dark background.

$description.$value: Status colors. NOTE: in dark, .strong tightens to color.X.300 (matches .icon) for better contrast on saturated backgrounds — this resolves the old alert.title divergence. A11Y FIX: info/success borders lightened one stop (.800→.700) to clear 3:1 against their bg; border pairs with bg, borderHover pairs with bgHover. CONSOLIDATION: status.*.icon is the canonical semantic icon color; icon.info/success/warning/danger are deprecated aliases.

bg.$description: CHANGED (2026-08-17): was color.neutral.850 (#202124). Moved one stop darker to neutral.900 (#18191B) per design request ("a bit darker") — mirrors the light-mode change (neutral.100 → neutral.0, both moves toward blending in rather than standing out). text (neutral.300, 10.12:1) and icon (neutral.400, 6.89:1) both still clear comfortably against the new bg.

border.$description: CHANGED (2026-08-12): was danger.300 (8.70:1 vs status.danger.bg — the value briefly shared with Light.json). Set back to danger.500 in dark specifically per design request. vs status.danger.bg (danger.950): 4.36:1, still well clear of the 3:1 non-text minimum. Light.json's status.danger.border stays at danger.300 (1.68:1 vs its fill) — the two modes are intentionally different values again here.

icon.$description: LINKED (2026-08-12): was danger.400 (5.97:1 on status.danger.bg). Now aliased to border.danger (danger.500) to match the rest of the family. vs status.danger.bg: 4.36:1 — still clears 3:1 with margin, just under the 4.5:1 text threshold if reused as text.

text.$description: LINKED (2026-08-12): was danger.400 (5.97:1 on status.danger.bg — comfortably AA). Now aliased to border.danger (danger.500) to match the rest of the family — vs status.danger.bg: 4.36:1. KNOWN AA MISS, accepted deliberately: just under the 4.5:1 text minimum (was previously passing). Fine for bold/large alert titles; check separately if used as regular-weight body copy.

$description.$value: Focus indicators.
Elevation aliases.
Chart series colors only.

Usage-limit meter bars (Billing & usage → Connections / Compute time / Data transfer progress bars). Mirrors Semantic/Light.json — same fill values, since the mockup uses one identical set of bar colors across both themes (only track/panel surfaces differ by mode). See Semantic/Light.json for the full rationale behind the 2026-08-28 recolor.

safe.$description: Was {color.info.500} inline. Same #009CC8 as Light — verified 3:1+ against both surface.panelInset (dark track) and surface.panel.

exceeded.$description: Was {color.danger.500} inline. Same #D34141 as Light — 4.11:1 on surface.panel (neutral.925), 3.61:1 on surface.panelInset (neutral.875, dark track). See color.danger.550 in Primitives.json for the full derivation.

track.$description: Unfilled portion of the bar. neutral.875 in dark — matches the mockup.

$description.$value: Switch off-state has unique values per theme.

trackOff.$description: Switch track in off state — in dark, the recessed look uses inputMuted (vs. border.stronger in light).

$description.$value: Reserved for the few cases where the Dialog component diverges from foundational surface tokens.

bg.$description: NEW (2026-07-23): Added for parity with the new dialog.footer.bg token in Semantic/Light.json. Dark mode's existing footer/body relationship is already correct — surface.panel (neutral.925) is darker than surface.overlay (neutral.850), so the footer already reads as the darkest layer under a lighter body. No divergence needed here; this just aliases surface.panel directly so it stays in sync with it automatically.

$description.$value: Nango semantic tokens — Light theme. Foundational semantic layer only. Components reference these directly; no per-component pass-through tokens.
Background and container surfaces.

raised.$description: NEW: lifted active surface (active tab pill, active toggle item). Same as panel in light, distinct from panel in dark.

overlay.$description: REVERTED (2026-07-23): briefly moved to neutral.200 to separate the dialog body from its footer, but overlay is the *whole* card's base fill — the header (title/description) has no covering frame of its own, so it sat directly on that fill and turned into a solid gray block across the top, which was not the intent. Back to neutral.0 (matching surface.panel) so the card/header reads plain white again. The actual body-vs-footer separation now lives entirely in dialog.footer.bg (see below), which only touches the footer strip.

$description.$value: Text colors.

muted.$description: A11Y RULE: do not use at fontSize.2xs (11px) or fontSize.xs (12px) — fails 4.5:1 on light surfaces (4.28:1 on surface.page). Use text.secondary at those sizes. See 'Accessibility note — text.muted at small sizes'.

placeholder.$description: NEW: dedicated placeholder-text token. Was reading as text.default/text.secondary in inputs, which made placeholder copy indistinguishable from real typed content ('too strong, confused with real text'). One stop lighter than text.muted so it sits clearly below every real-text tier (strong/default/secondary/muted) while staying legible — 3.36:1 on surface.input (#FFFFFF), 3.08:1 on surface.inputMuted. Intentionally under the 4.5:1 text threshold: placeholder is a hint, not required reading (WCAG 1.4.3 does not apply to it), but stays ≥3:1 so it doesn't disappear. Do not use for real input values, helper text, or error text — use text.default/text.secondary/text.danger for those.

disabled.$description: A11Y FIX (2026-07-09): was neutral.400 (2.34:1 on the disabled button fill — reported as unreadable). Moved to neutral.500 (same stop as text.muted) — clears 3:1 against the new interactive.disabled fill (neutral.100). Disabled-ness is still communicated by the muted fill/border and cursor, not by making the label illegibly faint.

linkNeutral.$description: NEW (2026-08-17): base color for the neutral/link-style button — alias to text.secondary so it matches what the component already rendered before this token existed. Added for parity with link/linkDanger/linkSuccess/linkWarning, which all have a named base token.

linkNeutralActive.$description: NEW (2026-08-17): active-state fix — previously default/hover/active all rendered as text.secondary with no distinct active feedback. Aliased to text.strong (neutral.900 light / neutral.50 dark) to mirror how every other link variant (linkActive, linkDangerActive, linkSuccessActive, linkWarningActive) gets a visibly darker/stronger stop for active. Contrast: 17.59:1 light (panel), 17.18:1 dark (panel).

linkDanger.$description: UPDATED (2026-08-12): was {color.danger.800} (2026-07-22, chosen for the extra safety margin — 8.02:1 on surface.panel). Re-aliased to interactive.danger (→ danger.700, 4.59:1 on surface.panel) so all three link-danger states track the button exactly and move in one direction — default .700 → hover .750 → active .900, all progressively darker. Fixes a zigzag Gaby flagged: with the old .800 default and the new .750 hover (added to match interactive.dangerHover), hover was LIGHTER/lower-contrast than default, so the link looked LESS emphasized on hover — backwards for a hover state. Still clears AA for regular text (4.59:1 > 4.5:1), but the margin is tighter than the old .800 — worth a visual check if this text is ever used bold/large only, since the .700 choice here assumes regular weight same as the button label. UPDATE (2026-08-13): the linkDangerHover token was removed (hover now renders with the default token), so the family is default + active only; both still alias the interactive.danger* button tokens.

linkDangerActive.$description: UPDATED (2026-08-12): now aliased directly to interactive.dangerActive (danger.900) instead of a separately-chosen danger.950, per design request that the danger link's hover/active match the danger button's hover/active exactly in Light theme. Passes easily as text: 13.91:1 on surface.panel, 13.32:1 on surface.page, 12.76:1 on surface.canvas. (Dark theme is NOT aliased this way — see linkDangerActive in Semantic/Dark.json for why.) UPDATE (2026-08-13): the linkDangerHover token was removed (hover now renders with the default token), so the family is default + active only; both still alias the interactive.danger* button tokens.

linkSuccess.$description: NEW (2026-08-13): success variant of the link/AlertButton family, mirroring text.linkDanger. Aliased to text.success (success.800) rather than a new stop — 6.60:1 on surface.panel, 5.93:1 on status.success.bg (the tinted alert surface an AlertButton sits on), both well over AA. Note success.700 (the stop that would visually match linkDanger's .700) only reaches 3.49:1 on panel — fails AA for text — which is why this aliases the .800-based text.success instead. No hover token: the link hover tokens were removed on 2026-08-13; hover uses the default token.

linkSuccessActive.$description: NEW (2026-08-13): active/pressed state for text.linkSuccess, darker than default per the one-rule-both-themes convention (hover/active never lighter). success.900 = 12.41:1 on surface.panel, 11.16:1 on status.success.bg. Matches status.success.strong's stop.

linkWarning.$description: NEW (2026-08-13): warning variant of the link/AlertButton family, mirroring text.linkDanger. Aliased to text.warning (warning.800) — 6.12:1 on surface.panel, 5.71:1 on status.warning.bg. The yellow ramp fails AA text everywhere above .800 (warning.700 = 3.94:1, .650 = 3.72:1 on panel), so .800 is the lightest usable link stop. No hover token (removed family-wide 2026-08-13).

linkWarningActive.$description: NEW (2026-08-13): active/pressed state for text.linkWarning, darker than default. warning.900 = 8.61:1 on surface.panel, 8.03:1 on status.warning.bg. Matches status.warning.strong's stop.

danger.$description: SWAPPED (2026-08-12): was danger.700 (4.59:1 on surface.input). Now aliased to border.danger (danger.500) per design request, so Input error label/description and the error stroke render as the exact same red. KNOWN AA MISS: danger.500 on surface.input/white = 3.83:1, under the 4.5:1 AA minimum for regular-weight text — accepted deliberately, not an oversight. SIDE EFFECT: Alert Title also reads from this token (see linkDanger note above) — it now diverges from status.danger.icon (.700), reopening the icon/title mismatch the 2026-07-22 move to .700 was meant to fix. Re-check Alert Title/icon pairing if that still matters.

$description.$value: Borders and dividers.

inputHover.$description: A11Y/VISIBILITY FIX (2026-08-12): was neutral.600 — only 1.79x the resting border's contrast against surface.input (3.36:1 → 6.01:1), reported as not enough visual separation between default and hover. Moved one stop further to .650 (7.93:1 on surface.input, 2.36x the default) for a hover state that reads as a clear, deliberate darken instead of a near-imperceptible shift. See border.input for the resting value.

danger.$description: FIX (2026-08-12): was {color.danger.400} (#F27474) — 2.79:1 against surface.input (#FFFFFF), failed WCAG non-text contrast (3:1 min). danger.500 (#EE4242) = 3.83:1, passes, and now matches Dark.json so the token can't drift apart between themes again.

inputDangerHover.$description: vs surface.input (#FFFFFF): 2.79:1 — under the 3:1 non-text minimum (same value that failed the original border.danger audit). Flagging since it's a literal value, not derived — worth confirming this is intentional for a hover-only state before treating it as final.

disabled.$description: A11Y FIX (2026-07-09): was neutral.100 (1.19:1 against surface.panel — no visible edge). Moved to neutral.300 so the disabled button silhouette is actually readable as a button outline instead of vanishing into the page.

$description.$value: Icon colors.

disabled.$description: A11Y FIX (2026-07-09): was neutral.300 (~1.6:1 on the disabled button fill). Moved to neutral.450 (~2.8:1 against the new interactive.disabled fill) — kept one stop lighter than text.disabled so icons stay slightly more muted than labels, per the existing icon/text hierarchy.

link.$description: NEW (2026-08-12): icon color for the link/button component's leading or trailing icon (e.g. the arrow in the 'Button' link). Aliased directly to text.link — not to a color primitive — so the icon always matches the link text color exactly, in every theme, with a single source of truth.

linkActive.$description: NEW (2026-08-12): active-state pair to icon.link. Aliased to text.linkActive.

linkNeutral.$description: NEW (2026-08-17): aliased directly to text.linkNeutral, matching the icon.link/icon.linkDanger/etc. convention so the icon always matches the link text color exactly.

linkNeutralActive.$description: NEW (2026-08-17): active-state pair to icon.linkNeutral. Aliased to text.linkNeutralActive.

linkDanger.$description: NEW (2026-08-12): danger variant of icon.link, for the destructive/danger link-button icon. Aliased to text.linkDanger so icon and text stay identical.

linkDangerActive.$description: NEW (2026-08-12): active-state pair to icon.linkDanger. Aliased to text.linkDangerActive.

linkSuccess.$description: NEW (2026-08-13): success variant of icon.link, for the AlertButton icon. Aliased to text.linkSuccess so icon and text stay identical, same single-source pattern as icon.link/icon.linkDanger.

linkSuccessActive.$description: NEW (2026-08-13): active-state pair to icon.linkSuccess. Aliased to text.linkSuccessActive so icon and text stay identical, same single-source pattern as icon.link/icon.linkDanger.

linkWarning.$description: NEW (2026-08-13): warning variant of icon.link, for the AlertButton icon. Aliased to text.linkWarning so icon and text stay identical, same single-source pattern as icon.link/icon.linkDanger.

linkWarningActive.$description: NEW (2026-08-13): active-state pair to icon.linkWarning. Aliased to text.linkWarningActive so icon and text stay identical, same single-source pattern as icon.link/icon.linkDanger.

info.$description: DEPRECATED — aliased to status.info.icon (now {color.info.800}, unified with text). Re-bind layers to status.info.icon, then remove this alias.

success.$description: DEPRECATED — aliased to status.success.icon (now {color.success.750}, split from text for contrast reasons — see status.success.icon description). Re-bind layers to status.success.icon, then remove this alias.

warning.$description: DEPRECATED — aliased to status.warning.icon (now {color.warning.650}, split from text for contrast reasons — see status.warning.icon description). Re-bind layers to status.warning.icon, then remove this alias.

danger.$description: DEPRECATED — aliased to status.danger.icon (now {color.danger.700} again — see status.danger.icon description). Re-bind layers to status.danger.icon, then remove this alias.

$description.$value: Solid fill colors for buttons, switches, selected states. Variants compose at the component level — no button.primary/button.danger split.

primary.$description: Unified brand-blue fill — same value used in Dark theme. White text (text.onBrand) reaches 4.78:1.

dangerHover.$description: FIX (2026-08-12): was {color.danger.800} — a 1.75:1 fill-to-fill jump from the .700 default, much bigger than any comparable hover step in the system (e.g. interactive.primaryHover's .750→.800 step is 1.32:1). Moved to the new color.danger.750 stop (added for this exact purpose — see its description in Primitives.json), giving a proportionate ~1.32:1 hover shift instead of jumping tonal registers. White text still clears AA comfortably (6.05:1, vs. the previous 8.02:1 and the default's 4.59:1). NOTE: this widens the hover→active gap (dangerActive is still {color.danger.900}) from 1.73:1 to 2.3:1 — left as-is since only dangerHover was flagged; revisit dangerActive if that gap also reads as too abrupt.

selectedFill.$description: Matches interactive.primary (info.750) so selected state and primary button read as the same brand blue. text.onBrand (white) passes at 4.78:1 — verified in both themes.

$description.$value: Global interactive state layers — applied uniformly across all components.

disabled.$description: A11Y FIX (2026-07-09): was neutral.50 (1.09:1 against surface.panel — fill was indistinguishable from the page). Moved to neutral.100 for a visible recessed fill; combined with the border.disabled and text.disabled bumps, the disabled button now reads as a muted-but-legible control instead of disappearing.

$description.$value: Status colors for badges, alerts, banners, and any semantic indicator. bg = surface, border = outline, icon = accent, text = body text, strong = headings/titles. A11Y FIX: text moved .700→.800 (body text needs 4.5:1 on tinted bg — .700 hit 3.31–4.28:1); strong moved .800→.900 to preserve hierarchy. ICON FIX (2026-07-09): icon was briefly unified with text at .800, which passed contrast everywhere but read as dark/muddy on light surfaces (reported: icons look 'very dark' in light mode vs. vibrant in dark mode). Icons only need the 3:1 UI-component threshold, not text's 4.5:1, so icon has been split back out to the most vibrant stop that still clears 3:1 on every light surface (page/panel/panelInset/status.*.bg): warning.700, danger.700, and a new success.750 stop (success.700 alone falls to 2.93:1 on panelInset). CONSOLIDATION: status.*.icon is the canonical semantic icon color; icon.info/success/warning/danger are deprecated aliases pointing to it.

bg.$description: CHANGED (2026-08-17): was color.neutral.100 (#EBEBEB) — a visible grey tint on the wide neutral banner. Moved to neutral.0 (white) per design request so the neutral banner reads as flush/blended with surface.panel and surface.canvas rather than a distinct grey box. text (neutral.700, 9.88:1) and icon (neutral.600, 6.01:1) both still clear comfortably; border (neutral.250, 1.48:1) stays a decorative outline, same as the existing danger-family precedent of not requiring 3:1 on borders.
A11Y/VISIBILITY FIX (2026-07-22): was info.50 (#EEFCFE) — nearly indistinguishable from white in light mode, reported as too dim. Moved to .100. text/icon at .800 still clears AA (5.68:1).

bgHover.$description: Bumped .100→.200 (2026-07-22) alongside the bg fix so hover still reads as a visible deepen. Now matches status.info.border (#A3E6F6) — border blends into the fill on hover, which is an accepted trade-off.

icon.$description: Icon color for info status. Unified with status.info.text at .800 — both pass 4.5:1 on white and on info.bg in light mode. Dark mode uses .400 for both (already unified).

bg.$description: A11Y/VISIBILITY FIX (2026-07-22): was success.50 (#F2FBF5) — nearly indistinguishable from white in light mode, reported as too dim. Moved to .100. text at .800 still clears AA (5.93:1); icon at .750 still clears 3:1 (3.53:1).

icon.$description: Icon color for success status. Split from status.success.text (.800) on 2026-07-09 — icon only needs 3:1 (UI component), not text's 4.5:1, and .800 read as muddy dark green in light mode. .750 gives 3.29:1 on panelInset / 3.93:1 on white — passes 3:1 everywhere while staying visibly closer to the vibrant success.700 green. Dark mode is unaffected (icon stays {color.success.400}, already vibrant against dark surfaces).

bgHover.$description: Bumped .100→.200 (2026-07-22) alongside the bg fix so hover still reads as a visible deepen. Now matches status.success.border (#C7EED2) — border blends into the fill on hover, which is an accepted trade-off.

bg.$description: A11Y/VISIBILITY FIX (2026-07-22): was warning.50 (#FFFBE8) — nearly indistinguishable from white in light mode, reported as too dim. Moved to .100. text at .800 still clears AA (5.71:1); icon at .650 still clears 3:1 (3.47:1).

icon.$description: Icon color for warning status. Split from status.warning.text (.800) on 2026-07-09 — icon only needs 3:1 (UI component), not text's 4.5:1. First moved to .700 (#A07B10, 3.30–3.94:1), then to .650 (#AC7C08, 3.12–3.72:1) per follow-up request for a less-brown, more-yellow read — .650 holds warning.500's hue/saturation and only darkens as far as needed to clear 3:1 on the tightest surface (panelInset). .800 (#7A5E0A) reads as olive/brown, losing the caution signal, which is what caused the original light-mode 'too dark' report. Dark mode is unaffected (icon stays {color.warning.400}, already vibrant against dark surfaces).

bgHover.$description: Bumped .100→.200 (2026-07-22) alongside the bg fix so hover still reads as a visible deepen. Distinct from status.warning.border (#FED75B/.300) — no collision here, unlike info/success/danger.

bg.$description: A11Y/VISIBILITY FIX (2026-07-22): was danger.50 (#FEF5F5) — nearly indistinguishable from white in light mode, reported as too dim. Moved to .100. text at .800 still clears AA (7.02:1); icon at .700 still clears 3:1 (4.02:1).

border.$description: CHANGED (2026-08-12): was {border.danger} (danger.500, 3.35:1 vs status.danger.bg). Set to danger.300 directly per design request — vs status.danger.bg (danger.100): 1.68:1. Below the 3:1 non-text minimum; consistent with this component's existing precedent of treating the border as decorative reinforcement (see Dark.json's border history) rather than a standalone status signal.

icon.$description: LINKED (2026-08-12): was danger.700 (4.01:1 on status.danger.bg). Now aliased to border.danger (danger.500) to match the rest of the family. vs status.danger.bg: 3.35:1 — still clears the 3:1 icon/UI minimum, just with less margin than before.

text.$description: CHANGED (2026-08-17): was {border.danger} (danger.500) — per request, aligned to the exact same reference as text.linkDanger ({interactive.danger}, danger.700) so the two tokens can never drift apart in Light theme (Dark theme's text.linkDanger and status.danger.text already both resolved to danger.500, so no change needed there). BONUS: this also improves contrast — danger.500 was a known AA miss (3.82:1 on white/panel, 3.35:1 on status.danger.bg); danger.700 clears 4.59:1 on white/panel and improves to 4.02:1 on status.danger.bg (still under 4.5:1 there, same accepted-for-bold/large caveat as before, just a smaller miss). TRADE-OFF: status.danger.text (now .700) now matches status.danger.strong (.700) instead of status.danger.icon (.500) — the icon/text pairing that was aligned in the 2026-08-12 change is now the one that diverges. Flag for a follow-up pass if Alert icon+title need to visually match exactly.

strong.$description: UNIFIED WITH ICON (2026-07-22): was danger.900 — moving icon to .900 earlier made it too dark, and leaving icon at .700 while strong stayed at .900 left icon and Alert Title visibly mismatched. Rather than dulling the icon again, brightened strong to meet it at .700. Caveat: .700 on the new .100 bg = 4.02:1, just under the 4.5:1 body-text threshold. This is fine if Alert Title renders bold at ≥14px (or ≥18px regular) — it then only needs 3:1 as 'large text' per WCAG, which .700 clears with room. Flag to design/eng: confirm Alert Title's actual type style meets that bar; if it's regular-weight and under 18px, this needs a different resolution.

bgHover.$description: Bumped .100→.200 (2026-07-22) alongside the bg fix so hover still reads as a visible deepen. Now matches status.danger.border (#FAC9C9) — border blends into the fill on hover, which is an accepted trade-off.

$description.$value: Focus indicators.
Elevation aliases for common container roles.

Chart series colors only — these are real assignment decisions (which accent maps to which series). All other chart visual roles use foundational tokens directly (gridline=border.muted, axis.label=text.secondary, etc.).

Usage-limit meter bars (Billing & usage → Connections / Compute time / Data transfer progress bars). Color communicates proximity to the plan limit, not the metric — safe/nearing/exceeded — the same bar recolors as usage climbs. UPDATED (2026-08-28): recolored per Erick's review — fills previously ran off color.info.500/warning.500/danger.500 directly (inline, not tokenized), which read as too saturated/alarming for something the user sees by default on every visit, well before any limit is actually a problem. Moved one full stop down the ramp for safe/nearing (.500→.600); danger.500 had no stop that both desaturated enough AND held contrast, so a dedicated muted stop was added (color.danger.550 — see Primitives.json for the derivation). All three fills are intentionally identical between Light and Dark (info.600/warning.600/danger.550 resolve to the same hex in both semantic files) so the meter doesn't shift hue with theme.

safe.$description: Was {color.info.500} (#00B2E3) inline. #009CC8 — noticeably calmer cyan, still unambiguous as 'in progress/normal'.

nearing.$description: Was {color.warning.500} (#F7C752) inline. #E6B738 — one stop darker/less lemon-bright, reads as caution without shouting.

exceeded.$description: Was {color.danger.500} (#EE4242) inline. #D34141 — the new muted meter-only stop (see color.danger.550 in Primitives.json). Do not substitute color.danger.500/.600/.700 here; those are ~20pp more saturated and are the exact look Erick flagged as too aggressive.

track.$description: Unfilled portion of the bar. Reuses the existing panelInset stop (neutral.100) rather than a new token — already the correct 'recessed well' surface for this and matches the mockup exactly.

$description.$value: Reserved for the few cases where form controls diverge from foundational tokens. Currently: switch off-state has unique values per theme.

trackOff.$description: Switch track in off state — divergent in dark mode (uses inputMuted instead of border).

$description.$value: Reserved for the few cases where the Dialog component diverges from foundational surface tokens.

bg.$description: NEW (2026-07-23): The Dialog footer and the card body it sits in were both bound to neutral.0 (surface.panel and surface.overlay respectively) — identical, so the footer had no visible separation from the body above it. Rather than changing surface.overlay itself (it is the whole card's base fill, including the header — bumping its value made the header a solid gray block, since reverted, see surface.overlay above), this gives just the footer its own token: same value as surface.panelMuted (neutral.25) — a tiny, deliberate step darker than the card, giving the footer a quiet strip of its own without touching anything else. Matches the relationship dark mode already has, where the footer (surface.panel/neutral.925) is a step darker than the body (surface.overlay/neutral.850). Dark mode keeps surface.panel directly (see Semantic/Dark.json) since that hierarchy was already correct.

$description.$value: Composite typography tokens. Theme-agnostic — identical in Light and Dark. Renamed from the old Body/* hierarchy. Distinction between text and label is line height (text = normal 1.5, label = snug 1.35).

xxs.$description: 10px / Regular / 1.35 LH / -0.01em — finest micro labels — use sparingly

xs.$description: 11px / Geist Mono Regular / 1.5 LH — small inline code

xxs.$description: 10px / Geist Mono Regular / 1.5 LH / -0.16em — finest mono (extra letter-spacing tightening intentional for legibility)

md.$description: 13px / Geist Mono Medium / 1.5 LH — emphasized code (was misnamed 'Body/Code/regular/md' — actual weight is Medium)

sm.$description: 12px / Geist Mono Medium / 1.5 LH — emphasized inline code

xs.$description: 11px / Geist Mono Medium / 1.5 LH — emphasized small inline code

xxs.$description: 10px / Geist Mono Medium / 1.5 LH — emphasized finest mono
